title: Card transactions with fraud flags, September 2026

findings.headline: Fraud is concentrated in night-time transactions
findings.detail: Night (0–5) has a fraud rate of 30.8% across 718 rows, against 0.3% to 0.7% at other times of day. Night is only 7% of volume, yet the overall rate is 2.7% (272 cases).

findings.headline: Fraud rate roughly quadrupled from early to mid September
findings.detail: The weekly rate rose from 0.6% (week of 31 Aug) to 1.7%, then 4.0% and 4.1% in the next two weeks. The final week, with 727 rows, is 1.8% but covers only part of a week.

findings.headline: Digital goods, online and low-value spend stand out
findings.detail: Digital goods has a 20.4% fraud rate (1,130 rows) against 0.3% to 0.7% elsewhere. Online is 6.3% against 0.3% for contactless, and amounts up to 535.9 run at 11.4% against 0.3% to 0.6% in higher bands.

findings.headline: Foreign AE and SG cards show very high fraud rates
findings.detail: AE is 28.6% (206 rows) and SG is 31% (187 rows), while IN is 1.6% and US and GB are below 1%. These two countries are only 3.8% of rows (2.0% + 1.8%), so a country rule would be narrow.

findings.headline: These patterns may overlap, so check before acting
findings.detail: Night, online, digital goods, low amounts and AE/SG may be the same transactions seen from different angles. The summary has no cross-tab, so the separate effects cannot be told apart.

next_steps: Cross-tabulate fraud by hour, channel, merchant category and country to see which patterns overlap and which add independent signal.
Review the 272 fraud cases from weeks of 14 and 21 September to see what changed from the week of 7 September.
Test a simple rule on night-time, online digital-goods and AE/SG transactions, and measure how many genuine transactions it would block.

reviews.note: Rates and the 718 rows check out. Removed the muddled 'yet overall rate' line. Night is about 221 of 272 cases (718 × 30.8%), roughly 81%.
'Quadrupled' is wrong. 0.6% to 4.1% is about seven times. Also noted the last week has only 727 rows, covering 28 and 29 Sep.
Digital goods 20.4%, online 6.3% vs contactless 0.3%, lowest amount band 11.4% vs 0.3–0.6% elsewhere all match the summary.
Rates and the 3.8% share are right. 'Narrow' undersells it: AE and SG hold roughly 117 of 272 cases (206 × 28.6% + 187 × 31%).
The summary has no cross-tab (cross is null), so overlap between these patterns cannot be separated. Medium severity is fair.

conclusion: Fraud is 2.7% overall (272 of 10,260 rows) but is far higher at night, online, in digital goods, in small amounts and on AE and SG cards. The weekly rate also rose from 0.6% to about 4% by mid September. Do first: cross-tabulate these patterns to see which overlap before writing any blocking rule.
limits: This review uses one month of summary figures with no cross-tab, so it cannot show which pattern matters most, why fraud rose, or how accurate the fraud flags are.
